name: Etherscan research: token holders, wallets, network health charts
goal: Use Etherscan (or *-scan clones) to inspect token holder distribution, trail early/smart wallets and what else they hold, and read Charts & Stats (transactions, unique addresses, verified contracts) for network health.

source.title: 3 Ways to Use Etherscan to Research Cryptocurrencies

outputs.name: research_notes
outputs.description: Holder concentration + wallet trails + chart snapshot

constraints: Educational self-custody/tax procedure only — not financial advice; no coin tips or return promises.
Ground every step in YouTube-provided captions; portable UI names OK when vendor chrome drifts.
Never digitize a seed phrase or enter it into a website/phone camera.
Research hygiene only — not a buy/sell signal; beware spoofed whale theatrics.

steps.action: Open the token page; review holders count/supply. Top holders: note % distribution; distinguish labeled contracts/pools from EOAs; flag microcaps dominated by one unlabeled wallet.
Open a top or early-buyer wallet (use oldest tx pages on smaller tokens). Review other tokens/protocols; watch the address or load into a portfolio tracker. Treat unknown rich wallets cautiously.
Resources → Charts & Stats: daily txs, unique address growth, daily verified contracts (dev activity). Note trend vs prior peaks.
Apply the same holder-distribution, wallet-trail, and Charts & Stats checks on the destination chain’s explorer (e.g. Polygonscan, Snowtrace) when the asset is not on Ethereum.
steps.expect: Equivalent research notes on the sister explorer
